ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The upper part of the figure gives the spectrum of M(f), which is nonzero only in two frequency bands: the negative-frequency band from -A to -B, and the positive-frequency band from B to A. The lower part is a block diagram of a modulation system: m(t) is first multiplied by v(t), then passes through a high-pass filter with cutoff frequency fc, then is multiplied by w(t), and finally passes through a low-pass filter with cutoff frequency fc to obtain s(t). Then reason: The support intervals of M(f) are [B,A] and [-A,-B]. The first multiplication by v(t)=cos(2πfct) produces shifted copies M(f-fc) and M(f+fc) in the frequency domain, corresponding to frequency bands [fc+B,fc+A], [fc-A,fc-B], [-fc+A,-fc+B], and [-fc-A,-fc-B]. Since fc>A, the high-pass filter has cutoff frequency fc and retains only the outer frequency bands with |f|>fc, namely [fc+B,fc+A] and [-fc-A,-fc-B]. Next, multiplying by w(t)=cos(2π(fc+A)t) shifts these two retained frequency bands again by ±(fc+A). The positive-frequency band [fc+B,fc+A] shifted downward by fc+A gives [B-A,0]; the negative-frequency band [-fc-A,-fc-B] shifted upward by fc+A gives [0,A-B]. The remaining shifted copies are at high frequencies and will be removed by the low-pass filter. Therefore the final output positive-frequency range is from 0 to A-B, and the bandwidth is A-B=100-40=60 Hz.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The upper part of the figure gives the spectrum of M(f), which is nonzero only in two frequency bands: the negative-frequency band from -A to -B, and the positive-frequency band from B to A. The lower part is a block diagram of a modulation system: m(t) is first multiplied by v(t), then passes through a high-pass filter with cutoff frequency fc, then is multiplied by w(t), and finally passes through a low-pass filter with cutoff frequency fc to obtain s(t).

Then reason: The support intervals of M(f) are [B,A] and [-A,-B]. The first multiplication by v(t)=cos(2πfct) produces shifted copies M(f-fc) and M(f+fc) in the frequency domain, corresponding to frequency bands [fc+B,fc+A], [fc-A,fc-B], [-fc+A,-fc+B], and [-fc-A,-fc-B]. Since fc>A, the high-pass filter has cutoff frequency fc and retains only the outer frequency bands with |f|>fc, namely [fc+B,fc+A] and [-fc-A,-fc-B].

Next, multiplying by w(t)=cos(2π(fc+A)t) shifts these two retained frequency bands again by ±(fc+A). The positive-frequency band [fc+B,fc+A] shifted downward by fc+A gives [B-A,0]; the negative-frequency band [-fc-A,-fc-B] shifted upward by fc+A gives [0,A-B]. The remaining shifted copies are at high frequencies and will be removed by the low-pass filter. Therefore the final output positive-frequency range is from 0 to A-B, and the bandwidth is A-B=100-40=60 Hz.
